name: chem-mc-plan-r1
context:
A PLAN FOR A MONTE CARLO ENGINEERING RUN, SUBMITTED FOR APPROVAL BEFORE ANY COMPUTE IS SPENT. Nothing here has been run. The request is to judge whether this is DESIGNED TO FUNCTION and PLANNED FULLY, and to reject it if it would produce numbers that cannot mean what they claim.

─────────── WHY A DESIGNED EXPERIMENT RATHER THAN MORE PROBES ───────────

Game two currently fails one shipping gate. AGENCY FLOOR is 4.1% against a required 25%: once a player reads the order book and takes every chance, there is almost nothing left to be good at. The measured cause is precise. An order is shippable on only 22.4% of turns (0.30 per turn) and the one-ply rule ships 0.31 per turn. It already takes every chance the instant it appears, AND NO POLICY MANUFACTURES CHANCES. The 27-30% gap to the beam search is foreknowledge of the order stream, not skill: a six-ply blind planner captures 5.5% of it.

Four candidate fixes have been tested, EACH ONE ALONE, and each was insufficient:

    order preview depth   -26.2% at 0, +3.2% at 2, +15.8% at 5. Real, not enough.
    transposition verb    at 120 kJ and a turn: COSTS the readable rule 18%.
    positional delivery   floor 2.4%, throughput halved -- and its ceiling was
                          INVALID, because the beam enumerates reactions only and
                          could not use the verb the rule existed to make useful.
    longer horizon        ORDER-1 3.03 and ceiling 3.97 at 12, 24 AND 40 turns,
                          identical, because the board dries by turn 8-12.

Testing one factor at a time is the thing that has failed four times. These factors interact by construction -- a swap verb is unaffordable at a 12-turn horizon and may be decisive at 30; preview is worthless without something to plan toward. A factorial design is the correct instrument and one-at-a-time is not.

─────────── THE FACTORS, FROM THE 115-IDEA SET ───────────

Ten dials, each traceable to a numbered idea, each already a config field or a small change to one:

    F1  TOPOLOGY    square-36 | hex-37                        (ideas 1-5)
    F2  PREVIEW     0 | 2 | 5 orders visible ahead            (idea 72)
    F3  SWAP        none | turn@120kJ | free x3 | modifier     (ideas 57-59)
    F4  BENCH       0 | 2 off-board holding cells              (idea 61)
    F5  POOL        rare5 | multistep-only | inventory-adaptive (ideas 62-64)
    F6  DELIVER     anywhere | dock row                        (idea 71)
    F7  OPTIONS     1 | 3 | 4-through-crucible                 (ideas 45, 49)
    F8  FIELD       none | local temperature | pressure         (ideas 67-68)
    F9  CONTRACT    plain | deadlines | tiered                 (ideas 33-34)
    F10 STREAK      1.00 | 1.15 | 1.35 multiplier              (idea 42)

Full factorial is 2x3x4x2x3x2x3x3x3x3 = 23,328 cells. At the measured cost of roughly 8 seconds per 40-seed gate evaluation that is about 52 hours for a single replicate and it will not be run.

─────────── THE STAGES ───────────

STAGE 0 - INSTRUMENT VALIDATION. Before any design question is asked. Three negative controls that MUST FAIL, watched failing:
    (a) a board with one molecule type must produce zero legal moves;
    (b) an agent handed a shuffled option index must score strictly below the
        same agent handed the true index;
    (c) a 'ceiling' restricted to the same verbs as the bounded agent must not
        exceed it by more than sampling error.
And one that must hold in EVERY cell of every later stage: CEILING >= BEST BOUNDED AGENT. An unbounded search can always play a bounded agent's move, so a negative solver margin is arithmetic reporting a broken instrument, never a finding about the game. This project has produced three such defects already -- a rollout scoring every ply against a stale book (-2.2%), the same rollout saturating at book size (-40.1%), and a two-ply agent whose follow-up list was the board's top-left corner (0%). All three were found by a number coming out wrong. Stage 0 exists so the fourth is found before it contaminates a 23,000-cell design.

STAGE 1 - SCREENING. A resolution-IV fractional factorial at TWO levels per factor (the extremes), 2^(10-5) = 32 cells, 3 replicates at different seed blocks = 96 runs. Resolution IV so main effects are not aliased with two-factor interactions. Response: AGENCY FLOOR primarily, SEED SHARE secondarily. Output: which factors and which two-factor interactions actually move the gate. Expected to eliminate at least half the factors.

STAGE 2 - FULL FACTORIAL on the surviving factors, all levels, expected 3-4 factors so 27-108 cells, 5 replicates. This is where interactions are read properly.

STAGE 3 - CONFIRMATION. The top 3 configurations by AGENCY FLOOR, re-run at 400 seeds each, on seeds DISJOINT from stages 1-2. A configuration that wins on the seeds it was selected on and not on fresh ones was fitted to noise.

STAGE 4 - EXPLOIT SWEEP on the confirmed winner only. Degenerate strategies (greedy energy, first legal, always option 0, biggest region, never swap, always swap), boundary abuse (out-of-range option index, duplicate cells, void cells, self-transposition, transposition with an empty bank), and a 5,000-round replay-divergence check that the executor scores submitted actions identically on replay.

STAGE 5 - POPULATION AND DUAL CONSTRAINT. The 15-persona population plus the full gate vector on the winner.

─────────── PRE-REGISTERED ACCEPTANCE, DECLARED BEFORE THE RUN ───────────

    AGENCY FLOOR     >= 25%      the gate currently failing
    SIGNAL UTILITY   >= 50%      the book is worth reading
    SEED SHARE       <= 35%      currently 53.9%; Farkle's is 3.3%
    SOLVER MARGIN    > 0         instrument sanity, not a design target
    DOMINATED        false       no thoughtless rule within 95% of best
    THROUGHPUT       2.0 - 8.0   orders per round, so the score is legible
    ROUND LENGTH     8 - 20 turns

NO THRESHOLD MAY MOVE AFTER RESULTS ARE SEEN. If nothing clears AGENCY FLOOR the honest report is that chemistry is a recognition game with a ~4% planning margin, and that goes to the user as a finding rather than being fixed by lowering the bar.

─────────── POWER, SEEDS AND PAIRING ───────────

Seeds are FIXED AND SHARED across every cell, so every comparison is paired and the deal cancels rather than being averaged over. Reported as paired deltas, not independent means -- with SEED SHARE at 53.9% an unpaired comparison would be mostly noise.

A pilot of 200 seeds on the current configuration estimates the standard deviation of orders-shipped. Seeds per cell are then set to detect a 5 percentage point difference in AGENCY FLOOR at 80% power, alpha 0.05, computed from that pilot rather than assumed. If the required n exceeds 400 the run is REDUCED IN FACTORS, never in power -- an underpowered sweep is how the Farkle staking gate produced an inverted result at 120 heats that vanished at 480.

─────────── COMPUTE BUDGET AND THE DEGRADATION PATH ───────────

Cap: 4 hours wall clock across all stages. Measured cost is ~8s per 40-seed gate evaluation after the partition memo. If stage 1 overruns, the declared order of sacrifice is: replicates first, then factor levels, then factors -- NEVER seeds per cell, because that is power. Every stage writes its raw cell results to disk before aggregating, so an overrun leaves usable partial data rather than nothing.

─────────── WHAT WOULD MAKE ME ABANDON THE DESIGN ───────────

Stated in advance so it cannot be rationalised later:
  - no factor combination reaches AGENCY FLOOR 25% AND the best reachable is
    under 15%: the core is a recognition game and should be reported as one;
  - the winning configuration requires OPTIONS=1, which would mean the product
    choice -- the mechanic this whole design rests on -- does nothing;
  - SEED SHARE cannot be brought under 45% by any pool or board-generation
    factor, which would mean the deal decides the game;
  - any configuration that passes only because its ceiling is invalid.

─────────── EIGHT ADDITIONAL STANDING INSTRUCTIONS I AM PROPOSING ───────────

These are recommended additions to the working method, not to this run alone:

  1. PRE-REGISTER thresholds and the stopping rule before compute. No threshold
     moves after results are seen without a recorded, separately audited reason.
  2. EVERY CELL PASSES AN INSTRUMENT CHECK or is marked VOID and reported as
     void. A void cell is never silently dropped, because dropping the cells
     where the instrument broke biases the survivors.
  3. DECLARE THE COMPUTE BUDGET AND THE DEGRADATION PATH up front, sacrificing
     replicates before power.
  4. HOLD SEEDS FIXED ACROSS CELLS and report paired deltas.
  5. FLAG ZERO-VARIANCE RESPONSES as suspected vacuous measurements. This
     project has hit that twice -- a correlation of 1.000 from a series with no
     variance, and a dispersion probe returning identical distributions for
     three different multipliers. The signature is a statistic that cannot vary
     with the thing it tests.
  6. RECORD THE LOSING CONFIGURATIONS, not only the winner. The negative results
     are where the falsification lives, and four of this game's five real
     findings were negative.
  7. A HUMAN APPROVER, NOT ME, signs anything that changes a gate threshold,
     marks a governance finding resolved, or flips a feature flag.
  8. THE RUN MUST BE REPRODUCIBLE FROM (seed, config) ALONE. Any hidden stream
     on the turn path is a blocker, not a caveat. This was already fixed once:
     a stateful rng filled cells a reaction left spare, which made the board a
     function of how many draws had happened and meant a beam could not branch.

─────────── THE SAME STRUCTURE, RE-POINTED AT GAME THREE ───────────

Darkmatter is a seeded universe rather than a board, so the factors change and the STAGES DO NOT. The plan for it is the same six stages, the same pre-registration, the same instrument validation, with factors over: dimensionality (3D vs a 4D slice), integration step and stability, procedural generation parameters, intervention verbs, observation horizon, and vertex-budget tiers for the GPU renderer. Its distinctive risk is different and must be added as a stage 0 control: a procedurally generated universe can be UNFAIR IN A WAY A BOARD CANNOT, because a seed can produce a universe with no viable strategy at all. So game three's stage 0 adds a VIABILITY ORACLE -- every seeded universe must admit at least one strategy reaching a declared floor score, checked before the seed is ever served, exactly as `drawReactiveBoard` already refuses a dead board.

questions.text: Is this experiment DESIGNED TO FUNCTION? Name the single most likely way this run produces numbers that look conclusive and are not.

Stage 1 is a resolution-IV fractional factorial, so main effects are clean of two-factor interactions but those interactions are aliased with each other. Given that my whole reason for running a factorial is that the factors INTERACT, is resolution IV sufficient, or does screening at that resolution defeat the purpose?

I pre-registered that no threshold may move after results are seen, and that if nothing clears a 25% agency floor I report chemistry as a recognition game rather than lower the bar. Is 25% the right bar for THIS game, or am I importing Farkle's number into a genre where it does not belong?

Four fixes were each tested alone and each failed. I am now testing them together. What is the strongest argument that combining four insufficient fixes produces a game that is complicated rather than deep?
Of the eight standing instructions I proposed, which is the weakest or most likely to be quietly skipped under time pressure, and what would you replace it with?

For game three: a procedurally generated universe can be unfair in a way a board cannot, so I add a viability oracle that refuses a seed admitting no viable strategy. What does that oracle COST -- what does filtering seeds on solvability do to the distribution of universes a player actually sees?
